searchText: My argument above is premised on the assumption that we want to move to SSZ in the EL everywhere *eventually* because it is better. excerpts.author: etan_status
excerpts.content:
And yes, `withdrawalsRoot` is the lowest hanging one because there is no migration needed for existing contracts.
Then, `transactionsRoot` to get rid of the inconsistency between CL / EL structures
Then, `receiptsRoot` to optimize other use cases
Then, `blockHash` / `parentHash` so that `ExecutionPayloadHeader` and EL block header can be made exactly the same (no more `block_hash`)
That then leaves only `stateRoot` as a hex root in the EL block header which is probably a different beast on its own.

Question is how to schedule. First one would be nice to avoid migrations (if we change anyway eventually no need to first introduce it with a legacy format.)
If the migration should be avoided, bundling with Capella is needed (and then the extra question is whether tx roots would be a real effort as well)

excerpts.content:
if we can get uniform buy-in from all of the EL devs (ideally by this Thursday's CL call) then im happy to update the EIP; although we should all understand that _any_ change at this point will lead to some sort of delay in the shipping timeline

specific changes:
1. withdrawal data is SSZ-encoded with the schema
```python
class Withdrawal(Container):
    index: WithdrawalIndex
    validator_index: ValidatorIndex
    address: ExecutionAddress
    amount: Gwei
```
2. withdrawals are encoded in the block as a `List[Withdrawal, MAX_WITHDRAWALS_PER_PAYLOAD]`
3. accumulator in the block header changes from the hash of the MPT to the SSZ hash tree root of a `List[Withdrawals, MAX_WITHDRAWALS_PER_PAYLOAD]`

excerpts.author: 0xrubo
excerpts.content: in general, we agree on having cl/el withdrawal roots match. but we think it's too late for this kind of change as it will delay shanghai delivery. not only do we need to implement the required changes for ssz adoption, but the ssz itself. it takes time to implement, test, fix, test, polish... also, withdrawals are a much-anticipated feature, and delaying it will irritate the community more. on the other hand, we understand that implementing it later has its own drawbacks. it's a pity that the idea came up so late.
